business.title: Long-term outcomes of avelumab maintenance in older patients with advanced urothelial carcinoma in Japan from the JAVEMACS study
business.description: The retrospective JAVEMACS chart review study described outcomes of avelumab first-line maintenance for patients with locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma without progression after platinum-based chemotherapy (PBC) in Japanese real-world practice. This post hoc exploratory analysis compared outcomes by age at avelumab initiation (<​75 vs. ≥​75 [main] and <​80 vs. ≥​80 years [supportive]). Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting estimated covariate-standardized associations; causal inference was not intended. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were assessed using unadjusted and weighted Kaplan-Meier and Cox models. Among 349 patients, 206 (59.0%) and 143 (41.0%) were <​75 and ≥​75 years, respectively. In the complete-case propensity score analysis set (n = 267), balance improved for most covariates, but some residual imbalance remained and overlap was limited. In the main weighted analyses, there were no statistically significant age-group differences in OS (HR 0.832, 95% CI 0.554–1.248; p = 0.372) and PFS (HR 0.794, 95% CI 0.577–1.093; p = 0.156); supportive results were also not statistically significant. These exploratory observations do not establish equivalence or an age-specific treatment effect, and interpretations should consider the retrospective design, complete-case weighting, limited overlap, and residual confounding. These findings provide descriptive long-term outcomes for older patients receiving avelumab maintenance in Japanese practice.

science.title: Determination of l-ascorbic acid and total vitamin C in cosmetic products using ion-pair RP-HPLC-DAD
science.description: Reliable determination of vitamin C in cosmetic products remains analytically challenging because of the susceptibility of l-ascorbic acid (AA) to oxidation and the complexity of cosmetic matrices. In this study, an ion-pair reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography method with diode-array detection (IP-RP-HPLC-DAD) was developed and validated for the determination of AA and total vitamin C after quantitative reduction of dehydroascorbic acid (DHAA) with tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP). Validation according to ICH Q2(R2) and Eurachem guidelines confirmed method specificity without matrix interference at the AA retention time. The limits of detection and quantification were 0.7 and 2.2 mg/g for AA and 0.9 and 2.8 mg/g for total vitamin C, respectively. The method showed excellent linearity over concentration ranges of 2.2–200 mg/g for AA (R2 = 0.9999) and 2.8–200 mg/g for total vitamin C (R2 = 0.9999). The method demonstrated good accuracy (recoveries of 95.99–110.31%) and precision (RSD ≤ 4.73%). Processed samples remained stable in the autosampler at 4 °C for at least 9 h, with signal changes not exceeding 4.5%. The validated workflow was successfully applied to ten commercially available cosmetic products, demonstrating its suitability for routine compositional analysis and quality control of vitamin C-containing formulations.

science.title: Structural basis and biochemical characterization of the Dicistroviridae 3C protease substrate specificity
science.description: Proteolytic processing of viral polyproteins by virus-encoded proteases is a prerequisite for successful infection and viral replication. In this study, we investigated the substrate specificity and potential cross-selectivity of Dicistroviridae 3C proteases by coupling in silico modeling of protease-substrate complexes with in vitro proteolytic assays. Structural bioinformatic analysis across distinct Dicistroviridae genera (Cripavirus, Triatovirus, and Aparavirus) highlighted dissimilarities in substrate accommodation. Despite structural divergences in the substrate binding cleft, a common mechanism for substrate stabilization near active site among 3C proteases was identified, explaining the prominence of glutamine at the P1 position. Feature analysis further revealed variations in the length of the β-ribbon, which likely acts as an additional determinant for substrate selection. To validate these structural models, we developed an in vitro test system utilizing active cricket paralysis virus (CrPV) 3C protease and engineered DnaK-based model substrates. Experimental validation confirmed that the residues at positions P2 and P4’ are critical determinants of catalytic efficiency and substrate specificity for CrPV 3C protease. These findings demonstrate that while the P1-stabilization mechanism remains conserved, structural variations in the β-ribbon and distal interactions dictate strict species-specificity, preventing substrate cross-processing within the Dicistroviridae family. Together, our work provides a structural and experimental framework for understanding variations in substrate selection among viral proteases.
